title: Crash between Alertmanager store.Set and the status patch can strand a config
description: syncAlertmanager writes the Alertmanager document to Mimir, then patches status with alertmanagerConfigHash/alertmanagerConfigAddress as the record that this Tenant owns it. A crash in between leaves the document written but unrecorded. Since Task 20's fix gates finalizer cleanup on that recorded hash, a Tenant deleted while in that state leaves the config behind with no CR describing it. Self-heals on any normal retry, because the next sync re-confirms via store.Get and records the hash. Found by Codex during Task 20 fix round 1 and parked deliberately: closing it needs write-ahead intent in status before the backend call, which is a design change, not a patch.

title: Missing basic-auth Secret wedges a deleting Tenant in Terminating
description: If a Tenant's BasicAuthSecretRef target is gone when the Tenant is deleted, backendOptions cannot resolve credentials, finalize cannot reach the backend, and the retry-forever policy keeps the object Terminating indefinitely. Probe-confirmed by the Task 20 reviewer; recovers as soon as the Secret is restored. The retry-forever policy itself is accepted and correct — this is a new trigger for it that operators will hit by deleting a namespace's Secret before the Tenant. Chart/docs task should cover it: document the recovery (recreate the Secret) and consider ordering guidance so the Secret outlives the Tenant.
close_reason: Documented in docs/migration.md Appendix B: recovering a Tenant stuck Terminating (recovery: recreate the basicAuthSecretRef Secret; ordering: delete Tenant before its auth Secret). Task 22.

title: Residual TOCTOU in finalizer ownership tie-break under simultaneous deletion
description: finalizeOwner()/claimants() read Tenants through an uncached APIReader and pick a deterministic lowest-name winner so exactly one of two colliding Tenants performs cleanup. A narrow window survives: if two already-colliding Tenants are deleted with sub-second overlap, both can observe the other as still present (or both as absent) and either double-clean or skip. Documented by the Task 20 implementer under 'Known accepted residual'. Closing it needs real cross-reconcile coordination (lease or a claim annotation), which was out of Task 20's scope. Impact is bounded: cleanup is idempotent deletes, so a double-clean is harmless; the skip case leaves backend state behind with no CR to retry it.

title: Enqueue peer Tenants when an ownership-key collision clears
description: When two Tenants collide on tenantId+backend+prefix, pruning is disabled on both and each reports RulesSynced=False/Conflict. If the conflicting Tenant is then deleted, or changes its (mutable) backend address, only that Tenant is enqueued — the surviving one stays Conflict with pruning disabled until its next resyncInterval (default 5m). Found by Codex during Task 19 fix round 1 (tenant_rules.go:213-216). Bounded and self-healing, and errs safe: nothing is wrongly deleted, and the arrival direction has no destructive window since a peer CR exists before its namespaces do. Fix: a watch mapper enqueueing affected peers on Tenant change. Needs its own design pass — a naive mapper amplifies every Tenant status write into a fan-out across all Tenants sharing a backend.
notes: Task 20 adds a sibling case: when the finalizer skips cleanup because another Tenant is the deterministic claimant, that claimant is not enqueued either, so it does not learn the conflict cleared until its next resync. Same mechanism, same fix (a peer-enqueue watch mapper) — resolve both together.

title: Recompute Alertmanager auth fingerprint after syncRules (TOCTOU)
description: syncAlertmanager resolves backend credentials, then syncRules runs a full List + POST-per-changed-group + DELETEs against Mimir before the second credential resolution. The window between the two resolutions is seconds, not microseconds, and is widest exactly when the backend is slow or unhealthy. Found by Codex during Task 19, parked by the implementer on a 'microsecond window' argument the task reviewer disproved. Impact is bounded: at most one resync interval of staleness, and a missing secret fails safe. Fix: have authFingerprint take backend.Options (it is Task 19's own new function, so no pinned signature blocks this) and recompute after syncRules.

value: In bash, 'set -e' does NOT abort on a negated command: '! grep -q X file' never fails the script, whatever the result. Every 'must not contain X' assertion written that way is silently inert. Found in alerts-operator's chart-test (an injected fake webhook config passed the no-webhook check). Use explicit 'if grep -q X f; then echo FAIL; exit 1; fi' instead. Same trap applies to any '! cmd' and to commands in a pipeline that is not the last element.

Never wait on a process with pgrep -f "<string>" when the waiting shell's own command line contains <string> — pgrep -f matches full command lines, so the wait loop matches itself and never exits. Cost us 87min: a subagent ran 'until ! pgrep -f "codex exec review"; do sleep 5; done' after launching codex, and four such loops deadlocked. Wait on the PID (wait $!) or match a pattern the loop cannot contain.
